title: BMZ Selects Minespider to Integrate Digital Battery Passports into EU Battery Production - Batteries News
content:
BMZ Selects Minespider to Integrate Digital Battery Passports into EU Battery Production
Every battery produced by BMZ Battery Solutions Group in Poland and Germany that requires a passport under EU regulations will carry one built from live production data.
Karlstein am Main, Germany, 17 November 2026:
BMZ has selected Minespider to implement Digital Battery Passports across its EU production in Poland and Germany, covering electric vehicle, light means of transport (including e-bikes) and industrial batteries, and building passport creation into series production rather than running it as a separate process.
The partnership gives BMZ and its customers a structured view of the information behind each battery. Product and manufacturer data, compliance documentation, circularity information and relevant operational data are organized around a unique battery identifier and shared through public and permissioned access, so each customer and partner sees the information relevant to them.
Minespider will support BMZ with battery data mapping, gap analysis, platform setup and passport creation, while working in parallel on integration with BMZ Group’s production environment. The implementation will begin with manual and batch-based passport creation before progressing toward API-based data exchange for higher-volume production, connecting battery data, unique identifiers and QR-code access more directly with BMZ Group’s internal systems.
BMZ expects the system to be ready by mid-December 2026 to handle the data required to create the first Digital Battery Passports. Under Regulation (EU) 2023/1542, from 18 February 2027 each electric vehicle battery, each light means of transport battery and each industrial battery above 2 kWh placed on the EU market or put into service must have a Digital Battery Passport.
Nathan Williams,
Founder & CEO, Minespider, said:
BMZ Battery Solutions Group operates at the point where Digital Battery Passports need to become part of production rather than an additional administrative process,
“By connecting product data, identifiers and BMZ Group’s internal systems with the passport platform, we are creating a practical foundation for the February 2027 requirement and for battery data that remains useful after the product leaves the factory.”
Robert Kowalczyk,
Managing Director at BMZ Poland, said:
Our customers use our battery systems across very different industries, but they increasingly need the same thing: reliable, structured information about the battery behind their product.
”We wanted one Digital Battery Passport approach that could work across our relevant battery categories and fit with the systems we already use. Minespider brings the regulatory and integration experience to connect that passport process directly with our production environment and give customers and partners the information they need.”
The same setup can support additional battery types and data sources as BMZ expands its implementation, giving the company a common basis for adding new products without rebuilding the passport process for every application or production line.
Christian Hasenstab
, Managing Director at BMZ Germany, said:
Digital Battery Passport is a significant step towards greater transparency across the battery value chain.
”As a European battery manufacturer operating across multiple markets and applications, we believe it is important to take an active role in this transition and ensure that our organization is prepared for the new standards shaping our industry”

HPQ Takes Another Step in the Commercial Deployment of Its Gen4 Cells by Unveiling a Nearly 2 kWh Power System Designed for Starlink Mini
An all-in-one solution incorporating 84 HPQ ENDURA+ Gen4 cells in a rugged case designed to power the Starlink Mini terminal off-grid and facilitate its storage and transport.
HPQ expects to make its first commercial deliveries between the end of the first quarter and the beginning of the second quarter of 2027.
MONTREAL, Nov. 17, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) —
HPQ Silicon Inc.
(“HPQ” or the “Company”) (TSX-V:
, OTCQB:
), a technology company specializing in advanced materials innovation and the development of next-generation processes, today unveiled the
HPQ ENDURA+ MiniMax
, a 1.95 KWh portable energy system developed to power the Starlink Mini satellite internet terminal
away from the electrical grid. The product represents a new commercial application for HPQ’s Gen4 lithium-ion battery cells, developed with its French technology partner, Novacium SAS.
Powering Connectivity Beyond the Grid
Designed to provide high-speed internet connectivity in remote locations, Starlink Mini offers a portable solution for outdoor activities, mobile operations, and emergency response. However, the terminal does not include an integrated battery and requires an external power source. With an average power consumption of 25 to 40 watts, maintaining connectivity for extended periods away from the electrical grid presents a practical challenge for users.
HPQ ENDURA+ MiniMax
addresses this need by combining HPQ’s high-capacity Gen4 lithium-ion cells with a rugged, portable power system designed specifically for Starlink Mini. With nearly 2 kWh of energy storage and an estimated operating autonomy of up to 80 hours, the system offers a practical solution for maintaining satellite connectivity in remote environments without relying on conventional electrical infrastructure.
Designed for the field
HPQ ENDURA+
, incorporates 84 HPQ ENDURA+ Gen4 lithium-ion cells, each rated at 6,500 mAh (23.4 Wh) in an integrated battery pack and a dedicated power output, packaged in a rugged case with space to store and transport the Starlink Mini terminal. The complete system weighs approximately 12 kg. Its design aims to simplify the logistics of carrying both a satellite terminal and its power supply, whether the destination is a remote campsite, a mobile worksite or a temporary emergency-response location.
Potential users include recreational vehicle owners, outfitters and guides, mining and exploration companies, oil and gas operators, construction crews, forestry and agricultural workers, remote field teams, defense personnel, and emergency services requiring reliable communications and autonomous power in off-grid environments.
The product is a third-party power solution designed to be compatible with Starlink Mini; it is not affiliated with or endorsed by SpaceX.
The new system draws on battery-pack design and assembly experience developed by HPQ and Novacium for drone applications and power solutions for French military radios. It also creates a direct route to market for HPQ ENDURA+ Gen4 cells through a finished product aimed at identifiable off-grid users.
Dr. Oleksiy Nichiporuk,
R&D Director of Novacium SAS, said:
For the HPQ ENDURA+ MiniMax, we adapted a battery architecture we already know well,
“We designed the system to power the Starlink Mini terminal off-grid, with a dedicated output and a rugged case that protects the antenna during transport.”
Bernard J. Tourillon
, President and CEO of HPQ Silicon Inc, said:
With the HPQ ENDURA+ MiniMax, we are opening a new and first commercial outlet for our Gen4 cells in the portable off-grid power market,
“Our agreement with Novacium gives us exclusive rights to commercialize Gen3 and Gen4 cells and the battery packs incorporating them in Canada, the United States and Mexico. We see this as a practical way to introduce the technology to customers across North America.”
Commercial launch plans
With certification of the
HPQ ENDURA+ MiniMax
in progress, HPQ plans to open reservations with deposits in early January 2027 and is targeting initial commercial deliveries between the end of the first quarter and the beginning of the second quarter of 2027. These dates are targets and remain subject to execution and market conditions.
Investors and technically oriented readers seeking further detail on the battery configuration, expected performance, illustrative market opportunities and commercialization rationale can consult the companion article: “
Inside the HPQ ENDURA+ MiniMax: Technology, Market Assumptions and Commercial
Strategy

title: Our Next Energy (ONE), America’s Independent LFP Battery Maker, to Go Public via Business Combination with Wen Acquisition Corp (Nasdaq: WENN) - Batteries News
content:
Our Next Energy (ONE), America’s Independent LFP Battery Maker, to Go Public via Business Combination with Wen Acquisition Corp (Nasdaq: WENN)
ONE is a U.S. battery company serving defense, rail, and grid customers from two factories
. The first, in Van Buren Township, Michigan, is America’s only source of large-format LFP cells built on domestic cell technology; the second, in Novi, Michigan, houses a pack line with 3 GWh of annual capacity. Both draw on secure domestic and allied supply chains.
The transaction gives the combined company a pro forma equity value of approximately $1 billion
: $600 million of pre-money equity plus up to $400 million in gross proceeds, comprising $300 million of cash in trust, assuming no redemptions, and a $100 million PIPE (private investment in public equity), of which $30 million is committed to date by two global strategic investors in steel and defense.
Cantor Fitzgerald is serving as exclusive capital markets advisor and sole placement agent.
Building on $40M of cumulative revenue, ONE has over $200 million in binding contracts
spanning multiple years with customers including locomotive OEMs serving four Class I railroads, among them Canadian National (CN), and five defense primes. As a 2026 winner of the U.S. Army’s xTech|Disrupt Endurance competition, ONE is eligible for follow-on government contracts without further competition.
NOVI, MI and NEW YORK, NY, Nov. 16, 2026 —
Our Next Energy Inc. (ONE)
, a U.S. energy storage technology company and battery manufacturer, and Wen Acquisition Corp (Wen) (Nasdaq: WENN), a publicly traded special purpose acquisition company, today announced a definitive business combination agreement. Upon closing, the combined company is expected to trade on The Nasdaq Stock Market LLC under the ticker symbol “ONEE.”
Most lithium iron phosphate (LFP) cells made in America today come from foreign-owned factories or rely on licensed Chinese technology. ONE uses its own domestic technology, from electrode active materials through fully integrated energy storage systems. Two recent federal actions make that distinction matter. The FY2026 National Defense Authorization Act (NDAA) extends battery restrictions to cells and components produced by a foreign entity of concern (FEOC) or under FEOC technology licenses. Executive Order 14421, signed in August 2026, restricts battery energy storage systems and other grid equipment tied to covered foreign entities from the U.S. bulk-power system.
ONE is uniquely well positioned to meet this moment. It makes its cells in Van Buren Township, Michigan, and integrates them in Novi with its own battery management systems (BMS) into packs and containerized energy storage systems for defense, rail, and grid customers that require safety, durability, and a secure domestic supply chain.
Mujeeb Ijaz
, Founder and CEO of ONE, said:
Over the last five years, LFP has grown from roughly 20% to 60% of the global battery market, yet China produces approximately 99% of the world’s LFP cells.
We built ONE to close that gap with a secure American and allied supply chain. We believe our combination with Wen will give us a public platform to scale ONE into this $40B addressable market with access to growth capital as we scale our operations to meet rising demand.”
Julian Sevillano,
CEO of Wen, said:
ONE has done the hard part of building an American LFP cell and pack business, with factories operating and customers in markets that increasingly require domestic supply,
“With two operating factories, binding customer contracts, and federal policy appearing to move its way, ONE is positioned to lead the reshoring of critical battery manufacturing in the United States.”
The boards of directors of both Wen and ONE have approved the proposed transaction, which is expected to close in the first half of 2027, subject to approval by Wen’s shareholders and ONE’s stockholders and the satisfaction of other customary closing conditions, including Wen’s registration statement on Form S-4 being declared effective by the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC),  the expiration or termination of the waiting period under the Hart-Scott-Rodino Antitrust Improvements Act of 1976, as amended (HSR Act) and the satisfaction or waiver of a minimum cash condition.

title: BMW GROUP OPENS HIGH-VOLTAGE BATTERY ASSEMBLY PLANT IN WOODRUFF - Batteries News
content:
BMW GROUP OPENS HIGH-VOLTAGE BATTERY ASSEMBLY PLANT IN WOODRUFF
AND MARKS THE START OF FULLY ELECTRIC VEHICLE PRODUCTION IN THE US
Plant Woodruff begins assembly of Gen6 high-voltage batteries for electric vehicles from Plant Spartanburg
Fourth site in Gen6 production network to start series production
Efficient production using AI and VR
Highest quality standards through consistent zero-defect approach
Local for Local: only 15 miles from Spartanburg vehicle plant
The BMW Group officially opened its new Plant Woodruff in South Carolina today, marking the start of series production. The facility will supply sixth-generation (Gen6) high-voltage batteries for installation in the new BMW iX5 and future electric vehicles at BMW Group Plant Spartanburg, which is located just 15 miles away. The iX5 is BMW’s first fully electric model to be assembled in the United States.
Electromobility is our most important growth area. That is why we are systematically electrifying our portfolio, with the US playing a key role: By 2030, we will be assembling at least six fully electric models at Plant Spartanburg. The start of series production of Gen6 high-voltage batteries in Woodruff is therefore much more than the successful launch of a new site: it lays the foundation for the first-ever series production of fully electric BMW vehicles at Plant Spartanburg and on the American continent. This marks the beginning of the next chapter in the success story of the largest plant in our global production network.
Raymond Wittmann, member of the Board of Management of BMW AG responsible for Production
Following Debrecen (Hungary), Irlbach-Straßkirchen (Germany) and Shenyang (China), Woodruff is the fourth site in the BMW Group production network to begin series production of Gen6 high-voltage batteries. With AI-supported production processes, digital twins and virtual reality applications, the new plant is setting industry standards for the assembly of high-voltage batteries.
Henry McMaster,
Governor of South Carolina, said:
BMW continues to deliver on its commitments to South Carolina.
Just a few years ago, I stood on this site with BMW leadership to break ground on this facility. Today, we are seeing that investment come to life and marking another milestone in BMW’s commitment to South Carolina. BMW has been a strong partner to our state, and this latest investment reinforces what we have built together and the opportunities ahead.
Robert Engelhorn
, President and CEO of BMW Manufacturing Co., LLC in Spartanburg, said:
We said we would begin assembling fully electric BMW vehicles in the US by the end of 2026 – and we are delivering on that commitment.
With today’s opening of Plant Woodruff, we are further expanding our footprint in South Carolina and strengthening the close integration of battery and vehicle production. High-voltage batteries assembled at this state-of-the-art facility will power the next generation of fully electric BMW X models from Plant Spartanburg.
Local for local: Five Gen6 high-voltage battery sites
Assembly of the Gen6 high-voltage batteries takes place at five new facilities, which the BMW Group built close to its vehicle plants, in line with its “local for local” principle. In addition to Woodruff, four more state-of-the-art high-voltage battery assembly plants have also been built: Debrecen (Hungary), Irlbach-Straßkirchen (Germany), Shenyang (China) and San Luis Potosí (Mexico). Gen6 high-voltage batteries have been series produced in Debrecen, Hungary, since October 2025. Plants Irlbach-Straßkirchen and Shenyang began series production in October 2026. Plant San Luis Potosí will follow in 2027.
Raymond Wittmann,
member of the Board of Management of BMW AG responsible for Production, said:
With the opening of our Woodruff plant, we are expanding our global Gen6 network: high-voltage battery assembly is now in place in Europe, Asia and North America.
This creates a key prerequisite for producing fully electric Neue Klasse vehicles on three continents. The rapid establishment of our Gen6 sites demonstrates the strength of our production network: we share know-how across locations and industrialise our new battery technology worldwide at speed. In doing so, we combine the strength of our global network with regional manufacturing, in line with our ‘Local for Local’ principle.
Intelligent production for maximum quality
The BMW Group has established state-of-the-art, intelligent and efficient production processes for its in-house developed Gen6 high-voltage battery. The new cylindrical round cells are integrated directly into the high-voltage battery, based on the “cell-to-pack” principle. All production steps are continuously monitored inline and comprehensively documented in real time. AI assistants and agents developed in-house analyse this data and, together with more than 300 employees and 250 robots at Plant Woodruff, help ensure zero-defect battery production. At the same time, the extensive use of artificial intelligence enhances Overall Equipment Effectiveness (OEE) in production. Well before commissioning, digital twins of production and virtual reality applications support planning and employee training.
Training in a virtual factory
All production staff at Plant Woodruff complete a VR training programme developed on site. Within a virtual factory, they can practise real manufacturing operations under realistic conditions. This virtual environment replicates the plant’s production lines in meticulous detail. The training helps employees develop an understanding of relevant processes and builds confidence in operating the equipment before they use it for the first time in actual production.
Following the official groundbreaking in June 2023, construction of the new plant began in September 2023. Just one year later, in September 2024, while construction was still under way, installation of the manufacturing equipment began, with the first test and pre-series batteries rolling off the assembly line in summer 2025.
Rich Everly,
Vice President Responsible for Manufacturing at BMW Group Plant Woodruff, said:
With today’s opening of Plant Woodruff, we demonstrate how quickly we can scale a new battery concept to industrial production.
The key factor here is the interaction between a skilled and committed team and the continuous sharing of experience within the production network.
Gen6 battery cells with reduced carbon footprint
The Gen6 battery cells for the BMW iX5 include a high proportion of secondary materials in their cobalt, lithium and nickel content. Renewable energy is also used in the production of anode and cathode materials, as well as in cell manufacturing. Compared with the Gen5 cell used in the BMW iX, CO₂e emissions have been reduced by around 28 percent per watt-hour. Plant Woodruff does not use any fossil fuels during normal operations, while the site’s industrial trucks are powered by hydrogen.
How the BMW Group builds its Gen6 high-voltage batteries
The BMW Group sources battery cells for its high-voltage batteries from leading cell manufacturers. The highest technical standards apply. Upon receipt of goods, additional measurements – such as voltage checks – are carried out. This is followed by so-called cell clustering, where the battery cells are connected to coolers. This step ensures optimal insulation and cooling of the cells. The cell clusters and cell contact system are then laser-cleaned and welded with pinpoint precision. The in-line inspection continuously monitors each weld seam in real time, while an innovative foaming process ensures that all elements are protected as a mechanical unit. The hardened foam guarantees the safety, stability and durability of the high-voltage battery. The housing is then closed, sealed and riveted. In the final assembly step, the Energy Master – the central control unit – is installed onto the high-voltage battery. Finally, each high-voltage battery undergoes a 100% end-of-line inspection. From Woodruff, the high-voltage batteries are transported to Plant Spartanburg, located just 15 miles away.

title: Redesigning Batteries for Ultrafast Charging EVs - Batteries News
content:
Redesigning Batteries for Ultrafast Charging EVs
Imagine charging your electric vehicle in the time it takes to finish your coffee. Chunsheng Wang is engineering a battery chemistry to speed charging times.
t’s hard to ignore the difference: You can fill a car tank of gas in mere minutes. Charging the battery of an electric vehicle (EV) can take 30 minutes or more.
Chunsheng Wang, a Distinguished University Professor of chemical and biomolecular engineering, and his team are working to quicken that time—a critical step toward shifting from the dominance of fossil fuel-powered vehicles to cleaner, more efficient electric ones.
If you want to compete with the gasoline engine, you have to have a similar charge time for the battery
The U.S. Department of Energy (DOE) is calling for the development of EV batteries that charge to 80% in less than 15 minutes. Wang and
Chang-Xin Zhao
, a researcher in his lab, are working to exceed this goal by cutting charging time to as little as 10 minutes—what they refer to as “coffee time.”
“That’s what we want to achieve.”
Solvents from electrolytes: The hidden barrier to fast charging
Previous efforts to expedite charging have focused on changing the structure of the battery’s electrodes, which inadvertently lowers the amount of energy a battery can hold—a problematic trade-off.
Wang’s group is devising ways to sidestep this trade-off by focusing on batteries’ chemistry. In research described in the journal
, his team, which Zhao led, identified a limitation lurking in the electrolyte, the medium through which lithium ions travel when a battery is discharged or charged. During charging, the ions move from the battery’s positive terminal to its negative one. But they don’t make the journey alone: Each ion picks up several molecules from a critical component of the electrolyte, its solvent, and drags them along.
If charging proceeds slowly, the solvent flows back into the porous material of the positive terminal, refilling it. During fast charging, however, the solvent can’t keep up: The electrode dries out, and charging slows down markedly. Chemists already knew about this phenomenon—called electro-osmotic drag—in fuel cells, but its occurrence in lithium-ion batteries had been overlooked until this University of Maryland-led study.
Wang (right) and his team perform innovative battery research in The Jeong H. Kim Engineering Building. (Photo by John T. Consoli)
Redesign the electrolyte to improve batteries
The team found they could reduce the risk of drying out electrodes by redesigning electrolytes.
They tested the modified electrolyte by constructing a small battery called a four-amp-hour pouch cell. While it’s difficult to get to a 100% charge without sacrificing other aspects of battery performance, the results fell within the DOE’s targets:
80% charge in 12.8 minutes
90% charge in 14.7 minutes
With continued research, Wang aims to reduce charging times even further, to 10 minutes. (Photo by John T. Consoli)
Ultrafast and long-lasting: Setting a new standard for batteries
Wang aims to reduce charging times even further, to 10 minutes, by combining the fluorinated solvent with a second chemistry-based strategy: an adaptive electrolyte his team has developed. This substance separates itself to protect both terminals from the stresses of fast charging.
Shortening wait times is only part of the goal. His team is also working to extend how long batteries last when not being used, and the temperatures at which they operate.
We want to build a battery that can satisfy all the requirements, without sacrificing anything,
“That is our goal.”

LI-S ENERGY SELLS FIRST CELLS FOR US SPECIAL OPERATIONS COMMAND EVALUATION
A first commercial sale that puts Australian-made lithium-sulfur battery cells in front of the world’s most demanding defence customer
Key Highlights:
First commercial sale of LIS battery cells: lithium-sulfur 10Ah Power Cells shipped for US Special Operations Command (USSOCOM) evaluation across crewed and uncrewed systems in the air, land and maritime domains.
USSOCOM is rapidly deploying battery-powered uncrewed systems where energy density and weight are critical to performance.
The US Department of War has requested more than US$74 billion for drone and counter-drone capability, the largest investment in drone systems in its history.
LIS lithium-sulfur cells enable uncrewed systems to fly farther, operate longer and carry greater payloads: a step-change over conventional lithium-ion.
Using no graphite, nickel or cobalt, LIS batteries offer defence customers a critically important allied supply chain.
Cells purchased on commercial terms by SOFWERX, the innovation hub tasked with fast-tracking new technology into USSOCOM operations.
Subject to results, further cell batches expected for platform-specific testing.
BRISBANE, Australia, Nov. 17, 2026 /PRNewswire/ —
Li-S Energy Limited (ASX: LIS) (“Li-S Energy”, “LIS” or “the Company”)
is pleased to announce the first commercial sale of its battery cells, with lithium-sulfur 10Ah Power Cells shipped for evaluation in support of United States Special Operations Command (USSOCOM).
The cells were purchased on commercial terms by SOFWERX, the innovation hub that serves USSOCOM. While modest in scale, the purchase represents early commercial validation of LIS technology and a funded commitment to evaluate its performance benefits.
SOFWERX will facilitate a project to evaluate the cells to identify capability advantages for USSOCOM’s crewed and uncrewed systems across the air, land and maritime domains.
SOFWERX is a streamlined pathway into US special operations
SOFWERX is a non-profit innovation hub operating under a Partnership Intermediary Agreement with USSOCOM, based in Tampa, Florida, alongside USSOCOM headquarters. Its role is to fast-track promising technology into USSOCOM operations.
It does this by hosting evaluations outside the traditional procurement system, giving companies a direct route to USSOCOM without the full complexity of conventional government contracting. For Li-S Energy, that means cells assessed quickly, on their technical merits, by the people closest to the operational requirement.
US Special Operations Command is the world’s most demanding customer
USSOCOM oversees the special operations forces of all branches of the US military. Its missions are among the hardest in defence: contested and remote environments, often far from resupply, where endurance, weight and reliability can determine mission success.
USSOCOM is rapidly deploying uncrewed and autonomous systems in every domain: aerial systems from micro-drones to long-endurance platforms, ground robots, and uncrewed surface and sub-surface vessels. Every one of these platforms is limited by its battery.
A measured, staged pathway to scale
A step-change in energy density translates directly into greater range, longer endurance and increased payload. With an energy density approaching twice that of conventional lithium-ion, LIS cells are well placed to deliver a significant capability enhancement.
Allied supply chains are also vital to USSOCOM. With less than 5% of battery-grade graphite and less than 25% of refined battery-grade nickel and cobalt under allied control, lithium-ion batteries carry major strategic and geopolitical risk. Li-S Energy batteries do not rely on graphite, nickel or cobalt, offering an allied supply chain with lower risk of disruption.
This first delivery supports an early-stage evaluation to identify alignment with prospective special operations use cases. If the results are positive, LIS expects to supply further cell batches tailored to specific platforms and mission domains. Any commercial outcome will depend on those results and on subsequent procurement decisions.
Technologies proven with US special operations forces are often adopted across the wider US military and by allied nations. With the US Department of War requesting more than US$74 billion for drone and counter-drone capability
, the market beyond this first sale is substantial and growing, and each stage of the pathway is designed to move LIS cells closer to it.
Dr Lee Finniear, Managing Director of Li-S Energy, said:
Our first commercial cell sale is a significant milestone for Li-S Energy, and there could be no better first customer.
USSOCOM is moving rapidly to uncrewed and autonomous systems in the air, on land, on the water and underwater. In every one of those domains, energy density and weight are decisive, and that is exactly where our lithium-sulfur cells are designed to excel.
Engaging USSOCOM through SOFWERX puts real cells in front of the people defining the next generation of these platforms. If our cells perform as we expect, the opportunity across USSOCOM and the broader US defence market is substantial.”
Brian Andrews,
Chief Technology Officer of SOFWERX, said:
Special Operations Forces operate at the very edge of what technology allows, and energy is one of the hardest constraints we face.
” As platforms become smaller, more autonomous and more widely distributed across air, land and sea, the demand for batteries that deliver more energy at less weight only grows.We are continually searching for advanced energy sources that can extend endurance, range and payload, and we look forward to evaluating Li-S Energy’s lithium-sulfur cells. If the technology delivers on its promise, advances like this could translate directly into greater reach and capability for the warfighter.”
The Company will keep the market informed of material developments in accordance with its continuous disclosure obligations.
This announcement has been authorised by the Board.

European industrial sovereignty: Veolia launches a pioneering site for extracting strategic metals from EV batteries
The key link in the value chain to strengthen geostrategic autonomy in EuropeA concrete commitment to building a sovereign and circular European value chain, ensuring a local supply for European automotive, construction and defense industries and, in the long term, with the support of public authorities, the manufacturing of batteries in Europe (“battery to battery”)A cutting-edge technology enables the recovery of more than 90% of the cobalt, nickel, and copper contained in the black mass resulting from battery shreddingA major potential market: nearly 700,000 tonnes of batteries to be processed within five years in Europe, representing an estimated value of more than one billion euros in strategic metals
Veolia is paving the way with a groundbreaking project to reclaim European sovereignty over strategic metals. The group is launching a pioneering initiative in the Grand Est region (France), in the presence of Estelle Brachlianoff, CEO of Veolia, Stéphane Séjourné, Executive Vice-President of the European Commission in charge of prosperity and industrial strategy, and Franck Leroy, President of the Grand Est Region.
Recovering strategic metals such as nickel and cobalt is a major issue of competitiveness and sovereignty for Europe, aiming to reduce its dependence on imports and to stop its valuable resources from being shipped abroad. Today, extra-European competition is driving a massive export of black mass to Asia. Yet within five years, nearly 700,000 tonnes of batteries are expected to be recycled in Europe, representing more than one billion euros’ worth of recoverable metals.
Guided by this vision, Veolia has brought to life this first European project equipped with proprietary hydrometallurgy technologies to process black mass flows from Europe (from France, the United Kingdom and Switzerland to date). The innovative process makes it possible to dismantle batteries, efficiently separate the black mass and, ultimately, extract cobalt, nickel and copper from it. These metals are then redistributed to the European automotive, construction and defense markets. Each year, the site will be able to recycle nearly 7,000 tonnes of black mass, the equivalent of 20,000 tonnes of batteries.
Pioneering in this field, Veolia is steadfastly pursuing its efforts to build a European battery recycling value chain. Several projects dedicated to battery dismantling, complementary to the processing activities of this state-of-the-art facility located downstream in the value chain, are currently being deployed in the United Kingdom, Belgium and Slovenia.
Europe’s backing is vital to securing a domestic supply of strategic metals. It is also essential for building a circular industrial model, by supporting the establishment of facilities that can reintegrate recycled metals. This calls for a Europe-wide regulatory and economic framework to be put in place now.
Estelle Brachlianoff,
CEO of Veolia, said:
Through its technologies and pioneering expertise, Veolia is helping to create a sovereign supply of strategic metals from recycling.
”Thanks to this facility, where European black mass flows converge, this extraordinary resource can be recovered within Europe: today serving the metallurgy sector and, tomorrow perhaps, producing new European batteries. This is the very purpose of our commitments and of the ambitions carried by our Green Up strategic programme: turning waste into a strategic resource and circular industry into a competitiveness lever serving local regions. The challenge is a collective one, on a key issue for our industry and our economy,”

title: Rock Tech Makes Major Lithium Discovery at Victory and Extends Exploration Trend to 16 Kilometres - Batteries News
content:
Rock Tech Makes Major Lithium Discovery at Victory and Extends Exploration Trend to 16 Kilometres
Significant discovery approximately 10 kilometres east of Bounty Pegmatite, extending Victory’s exploration trend from approximately 6 kilometres to 16 kilometres.
Surface exposure spans approximately 150 metres along strike and at least 60 metres across, with visible spodumene throughout.
Handheld LIBS analysis detected lithium in selected crystals, supporting field observations of spodumene mineralization.
New Discovery expands Victory’s exploration potential and accelerates drill targeting and planning.
New Discovery strengthens Victory’s role in Rock Tech’s strategy to build an integrated lithium supply chain in Ontario.
TORONTO, Nov. 16, 2026 /PRNewswire/ —
Rock Tech Lithium Inc.
) (OTCQX:
) (FWB: RJIB) (WKN: A1XF0V)
(the “Company” or “Rock Tech”)
is pleased to announce a significant new spodumene-bearing pegmatite discovery (the “New Discovery”) at the Victory Project (“Victory Project” or the “Project”) in Northwestern Ontario. The New Discovery was identified early in the Company’s ongoing field program, announced on October 22, 2026, and lies approximately 10 kilometres east of the Bounty Pegmatite. Next to Last Resort Pegmatite, the Bounty Pegmatite is one of two Victory Projects lithium-cesium-tantalum pegmatites (“LCT”).
The New Discovery reinforces the Victory Project’s potential to provide additional lithium feedstock within the regional transportation network serving the Company’s Georgia Lake project and proposed Red Rock Converter, supported by proximity to established highway and railway infrastructure in Northwestern Ontario. By adding a substantial third spodumene-bearing pegmatite, the discovery strengthens the exploration case for the Victory Project’s longer-term role in supplying Rock Tech’s proposed Red Rock Converter.
The New Discovery features a substantial spodumene-bearing surface exposure measuring approximately 150 metres along strike and at least 60 metres across, with visible spodumene through the exposure. Beyond the discovery itself, it extends the known lithium exploration trend from approximately 6 km to 16 km, opening a significantly larger area for exploration. While the continuity between the identified occurrences and the extent of mineralization at depth remain to be established, the discovery marks an important expansion of the Project’s overall potential.
Mirco Wojnarowicz,
CEO of Rock Tech, said:
“The New Discovery adds another important piece to the geological picture and a significant new dimension to our exploration potential. We are only beginning to understand what Victory may have to offer – and we are excited about what lies ahead.”
The New Discovery advances the exploration model
Prospectors Jason LeBlanc of Bounty Gold and Jace Angell of Last Resort Resources identified the outcrop while investigating priority targets generated through the field program’s geological interpretation and target selection criteria. The Discovery supports the team’s approach and provides additional geological information to refine the search for further spodumene-bearing pegmatites across the Victory Project.
Cameron Andrews,
General Manager Canada of Rock Tech, said:
Our crews, led by Bounty Gold and Last Resort Resources with support from Bayside Geoscience, set out to find new lithium occurrences along the six-kilometre trend and establish a basis for scale across the Victory Project,
“This New Discovery has delivered early success for the field program, identifying a substantial spodumene-bearing pegmatite beyond Bounty Pegmatite. The size of the exposed pegmatite and the presence of spodumene throughout make it a clear priority. Our next step is to establish how lithium grades are distributed across the exposure and use that information to guide drill design and testing.”
Previously announced field program continues
Rock Tech continues to carry out the field program outlined in its October 22, 2026 news release, including geological mapping and sampling at Last Resort and Bounty Pegmatite, evaluation of potential extensions and prospecting of high-priority targets. The New Discovery provides additional geological information to guide this ongoing work across the expanded exploration trend.
The program is intended to assess the scale potential of the Victory Project’s pegmatite system and identify priority targets for the planned maiden drill program in 2027. Rock Tech will release further assay results, together with its final observations and assessment, following completion of the field program and receipt and review of the results.
Sampling and Assays
Rock Tech submitted rock samples from the 2026 field program to Activation Laboratories Ltd. (Actlabs) in Thunder Bay. Lithium analyses will measure the lithium content of the sampled rock, reported as Li₂O. Multi-element data will help assess pegmatite fractionation and guide follow-up exploration for lithium-cesium-tantalum (LCT) pegmatites. Laboratory assays are pending.
Qualified Person and Technical Disclosure
The scientific and technical information in this news release has been reviewed and approved by Cameron Andrews, P.Eng., a “qualified person” as defined in National Instrument 43-101 — Standards of Disclosure for Mineral Projects.
On behalf of the Company,
Mirco Wojnarowicz,
CEO, said:
Current and historical grab samples are selective and are not necessarily representative of mineralization on the Project.
Historical results referenced at Last Resort have not been fully verified by the Company. Surface exposure dimensions and visual observations do not establish representative lithium grades, true thickness or continuity at depth. The approximately 16-kilometre exploration trend describes the span of known occurrences and does not represent a continuously mineralized zone.

title: Samsung SDI lands LFP battery deal with Jupiter Power - Batteries News
content:
Samsung SDI lands LFP battery deal with Jupiter Power
Samsung SDI will supply 16 gigawatt-hours of lithium iron phosphate (LFP) batteries to the energy storage systems operator for its large-scale projects in the United States.
Samsung SDI sealed a deal with Jupiter Power to supply 16 gigawatt-hours of lithium iron phosphate (LFP) batteries, the Korean battery maker said on Monday.
The energy storage systems (ESS) operator will use the batteries for large-scale projects in the United States.
The size of the deal has not been disclosed, but industry estimates put it at about 3 trillion won ($2.2 billion).
Production will take place at Samsung SDI’s plant in Indiana, and delivery will take place over three years starting in 2029.
Jupiter Power — owned by BlackRock, the global asset manager, and based in Austin, Texas — has one of the largest ESS project pipelines in the United States.
Samsung SDI’s Indiana factory, which was initially planned as a joint venture with General Motors focused on EV batteries, turned into an LFP battery production line for ESS after the Korean battery maker acquired a 100 percent share in the plant.
Samsung SDI is currently the only non-Chinese maker of prismatic ESS batteries in North America.
Combining the newly inked agreement with earlier orders between the two companies, the total supply comes to roughly 27 gigawatt-hours.
The contract also adds to a run of U.S. orders for Samsung SDI, which secured an ESS LFP supply deal worth more than 2 trillion won late last year. It agreed to a 1.5 trillion won ESS battery deal with a U.S. energy company in March, as well as a 1-gigawatt-hour ESS supply contract with Alpha Omega Power last month.

Coreshell Technologies Raises $30M Series B to Scale China-Free Batteries for US Industries
SAN LEANDRO, Calif., Nov. 11, 2026 /PRNewswire/ —
Coreshell Technologies
, a battery technology company, today announced the close of a $30 million Series B financing round co-led by
Ferroglobe
PLC (NASDAQ:
Access Industries
, with participation from
Helios Ventures
Pegasus Tech Ventures
, Mana Ventures, and
Entrada Ventures
. The funding will accelerate the commercialization and scale-up of Coreshell’s battery technology, support expansion of manufacturing and customer programs, and advance its goal of eliminating dependence on China for critical battery materials across both the anode and cathode supply chains.
This round builds on significant public-sector support for Coreshell’s domestic battery manufacturing efforts, including a
$50 million grant from the Department of Energy
in August.
The financing comes as U.S. manufacturers across defense, automotive, data centers, and other key industries look to strengthen supply-chain resilience and secure access to domestic sources of critical materials. Federal sourcing requirements, including those under the National Defense Authorization Act (NDAA), along with new procurement policies and
White House measures
, are accelerating that shift, particularly in defense, where compliance alone may not protect manufacturers from supply-chain disruptions.
Graphite is a critical component of conventional lithium-ion batteries,
and more than 90 percent of the world’s graphite
is processed in China. This concentration leaves battery manufacturers and their customers vulnerable to disruptions beyond their control.
In 2023, China
tightened controls on graphite exports
, underscoring the risks of relying on a concentrated source for a critical battery material. Coreshell eliminates that vulnerability by replacing graphite entirely with metallurgical silicon (MGS), a widely available, low-cost material produced in the US.
Jonathan Tan,
CEO and Co-Founder of Coreshell Technologies, said:
Meeting sourcing requirements is an important step, but it doesn’t necessarily mean a battery supply chain is secure, no matter what industry you’re in
“This new financing gives us the resources to scale a battery supply chain that eliminates dependence on China for critical materials while delivering advantages in performance and cost.”
That effort is already underway. Coreshell is using its $50 million federal grant to build the first giga-scale factory for cells using MGS anodes, vastly expanding domestic production of this critical battery technology.
Dave Bellis
, Manager of Corporate Strategy and Development at ADS, the top supplier to the Defense Logistics Agency, said:
As uncrewed systems become increasingly important to the future of American defense, the batteries powering those systems cannot be a geopolitical liability
“Coreshell has a differentiated technology and a supply chain designed around domestic critical minerals, giving the defense industry a path toward batteries that are both high-performing and genuinely secure.”
A Battery Technology Built Around Domestic Materials
Coreshell replaces conventional graphite with metallurgical silicon (MGS), a raw, commercially produced form of silicon that differs from the expensive, silane-based materials used in other silicon-anode cells. Coreshell’s MGS anode leverages silicon’s performance and cost advantages while using an abundant, domestically sourced material. On the cathode side, an
agreement with L&F Co., Ltd
provides long-term access to lithium, enabling Coreshell to produce batteries free of Chinese critical materials.

title: Sub-Millisecond Battery Converter Gives 800 VDC AI Data Centers More Compute from the Same Grid Connection - Batteries News
content:
Sub-Millisecond Battery Converter Gives 800 VDC AI Data Centers More Compute from the Same Grid Connection
FORT COLLINS, Colo., Nov. 11, 2026 /PRNewswire/ — Ampt’s new Battery Converter helps AI data centers run more compute per megawatt of grid capacity as they transition to 800 VDC architectures. The converter delivers regulated 800 VDC from a DC bus shared by battery storage and grid or on-site power, providing active power conditioning that responds to GPU load changes in less than 1 millisecond. With the battery handling short peaks, GPUs can run without power capping and the grid connection can be sized for average load rather than peak load. Each 2U rack-mountable unit delivers 80 kW (100 A), and units can be paralleled from a single rack to a full row or an entire GPU cluster. The Battery Converter is currently in partner pilots for data centers, with general availability in Q3 2027.
Why Does Millisecond Response Matter?
Data centers are moving to 800 VDC power architectures for rack-scale AI systems, which are
projected
to support 1 MW IT racks and improve end-to-end power efficiency by up to 5% compared with 54 V systems, according to NVIDIA. AI workloads can swing a rack’s power draw between 30% and 100% within milliseconds. The grid needs a steady, predictable load, while the GPUs need a highly dynamic source. NVIDIA’s white paper says energy storage “needs to fill the gap between these two conflicting requirements.”
How Does the Battery Converter Work?
In Ampt’s design, the battery, the grid and any on-site generation all feed a common DC bus. The Battery Converter steps that bus down to a regulated 800 VDC supply for the GPU racks. When GPU load changes, the Ampt converter responds in less than 1 millisecond, enabling the battery to supply or absorb the difference while the grid or on-site generation sees steadier demand. Smoothing these peaks lets operators size upstream power equipment closer to average demand, reducing equipment costs, while presenting a steadier load that can help sites secure timely grid access.
The grid connects to the DC bus through a medium-voltage transformer and power conversion system, and feeds batteries that operate up to 1500 VDC. With a grid-forming power conversion system, the battery that absorbs GPU swings can also actively support grid voltage and frequency. These are the same transformers, power conversion systems and batteries used in utility-scale storage today, so data center operators can build on established supply chains and on the nearly two decades Ampt has spent deploying DC power conversion for utility-scale solar and energy storage systems.
How Does the Design Improve Efficiency?
In a power-limited AI factory, every kilowatt lost in conversion and distribution is capacity that cannot run GPUs, and operators pay for it twice, once as electricity and again as cooling. To keep more of that power for compute, Ampt’s design reduces losses in the converter, in storage and in distribution. The Ampt Battery Converter reaches up to 99.2% peak efficiency. Stored energy stays DC, avoiding the costly DC-to-AC-to-DC conversions of AC-coupled storage. And the DC bus feeding the converters runs at 1100 to 1500 VDC, depending on the battery’s state of charge, with the converters delivering a stable 800 VDC to the GPU racks. Higher voltage carries the same power at lower current, which reduces conductor losses or allows smaller conductors. Ampt’s Battery Converter is built for the first generation of 800 VDC racks while delivering the benefits of higher distribution voltages that appear only on future roadmaps.
How Does the Converter Scale?
Ampt Battery Converter units can be paralleled to any power level, allowing the same 2U, 80 kW (100 A) building block to serve a single GPU rack, a full row or an entire data hall. Adding one unit provides N+1 redundancy, maintaining full power if a unit goes offline. Sites with existing or planned solar can also connect PV systems to the same battery DC bus through Ampt String Optimizers, with no additional inverter or transformer.
Aaron Gomolak,
CEO of Ampt, said:
In AI factories, GPU loads swing in milliseconds, so storage has to work every minute of the day.
”With the Ampt Battery Converter, the same battery gives the grid a steady load and the GPUs the fast-responding power they need. For operators, that means reliable compute and a faster path to bringing new AI capacity online. For the communities around them, it means data centers that are easier on the grid,”

title: Ampace to Highlight Safety and Space Efficiency in UPS Battery Solutions at Data Centre World Paris 2026 - Batteries News
content:
Ampace to Highlight Safety and Space Efficiency in UPS Battery Solutions at Data Centre World Paris 2026
PARIS, Nov. 11, 2026 /PRNewswire/ — Ampace, a global provider of lithium-ion battery solutions, will showcase its PU200 UPS battery solution at Data Centre World Paris 2026, taking place November 18–19 at Paris Expo Porte de Versailles. With a comprehensive portfolio of battery technologies and solutions for AI data centers (AIDC), Ampace supports critical power infrastructure needs, from battery cells to integrated backup power systems. At
Hall 5, Booth M65
, the company will present the PU200’s safety features and compact design for data center backup power applications.
As AI adoption accelerates across Europe, higher-density computing environments are placing greater demands on critical power infrastructure. For data center operators, planning backup power involves balancing reliable performance, battery
system safety and the efficient use
of available space. These considerations are shaping the evaluation of UPS battery solutions for data center applications.
Safety from Cell to System
For European data center operators, battery safety is a key consideration in maintaining resilient, mission-critical infrastructure. The PU200 combines semi-solid-state battery technology with module-level and cabinet-level fire protection. These features bring together cell technology and protection at multiple levels of the battery system, making safety a central consideration in its design.
For operators evaluating lithium-ion batteries for critical backup applications, both cell characteristics and system-level protection are relevant considerations. The PU200 incorporates these elements within its UPS battery solution for data center applications.
High-Power Backup in a Compact Footprint
The PU200 combines high-rate discharge capability with a compact cabinet design. With a power output of
462 kW/cabinet
, it is designed to support high-power backup requirements while making efficient use of space allocated to UPS batteries.
For operators planning high-density facilities, this combination can help address the challenge of accommodating backup power infrastructure within constrained layouts. A quick-detachable battery management system also helps simplify servicing. The solution supports installation in both traditional and modular data center configurations, providing options for different facility layouts.
Through its participation in Data Centre World Paris 2026, Ampace looks forward to exchanging insights with data center operators, infrastructure partners and industry experts on safety and space efficiency in data center backup power.
Ampace at Hall 5, Booth M65
, to learn more about the PU200 and discuss data center backup power requirements.

title: Appear Inc Begins Pre Production of Solid-State Battery, Targets Mid-2027 Launch - Batteries News
content:
Appear Inc Begins Pre Production of Solid-State Battery, Targets Mid-2027 Launch
Field trials complete across motorcycles, e-bikes and scooters. Pre-production underway. Limited production on track for mid-2027, with full-scale production in 2028.
SAN FRANCISCO, Nov. 10, 2026 /PRNewswire/ — Appear Inc., a San Francisco-based developer of next-generation solid-state battery technology, today announced that it has moved from proving its technology to producing it.
The company has completed field trials on three types of electric vehicle: motorcycles, e-bikes and scooters. It has also completed advanced manufacturing trials and started pre-production manufacturing with a manufacturing partner.
Alongside this technical progress, Appear has added new distributors and strategic partners in selective established and emerging markets. The company remains on track to begin limited commercial production in mid-2027, followed by full-scale production in 2028.
The technology
Most electric vehicles today run on lithium-ion batteries, which use a liquid electrolyte to move charge between the electrodes. Solid-state batteries replace that liquid with a solid material. This is widely seen as a path to safer batteries, with no flammable liquid to leak or ignite, and to more energy in a smaller, lighter cell.
Appear’s solid-state technology is built around three priorities: safety, performance and manufacturability. For motorcycles, e-bikes and scooters, where weight, range and safety matter on every ride, that combination is especially valuable.
Following its advanced manufacturing trials, Appear has moved into pre-production with its manufacturing partner and is refining its processes for volume manufacturing.
Building a route to market
New distributors and strategic partners in selective established and emerging markets are expected to give Appear regional market access and distribution channels at launch. Partner details remain confidential.
Prashant Rurs,
Founder & CEO of Appear Inc, said:
We are moving beyond development and validation and into commercialization,
“We remain on track to begin limited production in mid-2027 and to scale up to full production in 2028.”

title: Höegh taps BYD batteries for ammonia powered car carrier - Batteries News

Höegh taps BYD batteries for ammonia powered car carrier
Norwegian car carrier operator Höegh Autoliners has signed a deal with Chinese battery giant BYD to install energy storage technology aboard an ammonia-capable newbuilding, bringing together four different energy technologies on a deepsea vessel.
The agreement, signed at the COP31 climate summit in Antalya, Turkey, will see BYD supply a marine battery system for Aurora No. 12, scheduled for delivery in May 2028. The 9,100 ceu vessel will combine ammonia propulsion capability, battery storage, solar panels and a shaft generator in an integrated energy system designed to improve efficiency and reduce fuel consumption.
Höegh estimates the combination will cut greenhouse gas emissions by approximately 1,000 tonnes of CO2 equivalent annually while lowering operating costs.
Höegh Autoliners CEO
Andreas Enger
We are combining every green technology available on one vessel capable of running on ammonia from day one.
”Nobody has done that on a deep-sea car carrier before,”
The Norwegian operator is positioning the ship as a testbed for integrating alternative fuels with battery technology on large ocean-going vessels. BYD’s containerised battery system will work alongside the ship’s other energy sources to optimise power management.
Höegh’s Aurora-class vessels are being built at China Merchants Heavy Industry in Jiangsu. The company claims the design can reduce carbon emissions per vehicle transported by up to 58% compared with conventional car carriers.
The latest agreement follows Höegh’s August order for six additional vessels, taking the Aurora newbuilding programme to 18 ships. Options and reserved construction slots could eventually expand the series to 26 vessels.

title: Amflow launches its first city e-bikes, packing huge torque and serious smart tech
content:
Micah Toll
| Nov 18 2026 - 7:55 am PT
Amflow has made a name for itself in the electric mountain bike world with its
high-performance Avinox-powered machines
, but now the company is bringing that same technology to a decidedly more urban environment. The newly unveiled Amflow UE Carbon series marks the brand’s first move into the commuter e-bike market, combining a lightweight carbon fiber frame, powerful mid-drive motor, and a surprisingly long list of smart features designed for everyday riding.
And while these might look like fairly conventional step-through city bikes at first glance, there’s some seriously impressive technology hiding beneath those clean lines.
Mountain bike power meets city bike practicality
Amflow UE series
comes in two versions, the UE Carbon and the higher-end UE Carbon Pro, both built around a full-carbon fiber frame weighing just 2.35 kg (5.2 lb).
The complete bike weighs as little as 20.9 kg (46 lb), which is fairly impressive considering the amount of hardware Amflow has packed into it, including front suspension, a suspension dropper seatpost, integrated lighting, and cargo racks.
Both models use the Avinox M2 mid-drive motor, which delivers up to 125 Nm of torque. That’s an enormous amount of torque for a city bike, and should make short work of steep hills, especially when carrying groceries or other cargo. And to put things into perspective, a lot of city e-bikes have barely 60 Nm for torque, so Amflow is knocking it out of the park for urban power.
A removable 600 Wh battery provides a claimed maximum range of 132 km (82 miles) in the lowest power assist mode, while fast charging can refill the battery in just 2 hours and 23 minutes.
The bikes also feature Avinox’s intelligent traction control system and a new Auto Boost function that automatically provides additional assistance when the system detects demanding conditions, such as accelerating from a stop or climbing a steep hill.
In other words, riders get much of the sophisticated motor technology developed for high-performance electric mountain bikes, but in a package designed for commuting to work or picking up groceries.
The bike is listed as weighing 20.9 kg (46 lb), though that figure conveniently excludes the front and rear racks, mudguards, pedals, kickstand, bike lock, bottle cage, and chainguard. So figure a few extra pounds for all of that gear, and you’re in the right ballpark.
Two drivetrains, plenty of technology
The main difference between the two models is their drivetrain.
The higher-end UE Carbon Pro ($3,899) uses a customized three-speed electronically shifted internally geared hub paired with a Gates carbon belt drive. That should make it particularly appealing to commuters who want a quiet, clean, low-maintenance setup without worrying about chain lubrication or derailleur adjustments.
The more affordable UE Carbon ($3,499) instead uses a 10-speed electronic derailleur developed with TRP.
Both models support automatic shifting, allowing the bike to handle gear changes without requiring the rider to constantly think about them.
Amflow has also gone fairly wild with the technology integration.
There’s a 1.4-inch touchscreen display mounted on the handlebars, a wireless phone charging mount offering 15W wireless charging or 20W USB-C charging, and integrated lighting with automatic low-light activation and brake-sensing functionality.
Automatic lighting turns on as soon as the sun starts dipping, ensuring you never forget to turn on your lights
The bikes even include a hardened steel frame lock on the rear wheel, Apple Find My integration, and a Lost Mode feature that can lock down certain components if the bike is stolen.
Apple Watch connectivity allows riders to check their bike’s status and unlock it, while heart-rate-based assistance can automatically adjust motor output to help riders maintain a target heart rate zone.
Some of these features, like the security and tracking, are immediately effective for nearly all riders, while other high-tech features like the heart rate-based pedal assist can provide even more functionality for niche riders looking to bridge the gap between riding for transportation and riding for fitness.
Designed for actually getting things done
Of course, all the fancy technology in the world doesn’t mean much if a commuter bike can’t handle everyday errands.
Fortunately, Amflow appears to have taken the practical side seriously.
The bikes feature a low step-through frame, upright riding position, 65 mm suspension fork, and a suspension dropper seatpost offering 125 mm of height adjustment and approximately 30 mm of suspension travel.
The 26×2.0-inch Maxxis tires should also provide a comfortable ride over less-than-perfect city streets.
There’s a front rack rated for 20 kg (44 lb) and a rear rack rated for 27 kg (59.5 lb), with the latter supporting the MIK HD mounting system for compatible accessories, including child seats.
The standard frame is designed to accommodate riders from 155 to 190 cm (5’1” to 6’3”), while a smaller version for riders down to 140 cm (4’7”) is expected in 2027.
Electrek’s Take
I’ve been impressed with the technology coming out of the Avinox ecosystem, and it’s exciting to see that technology finally make its way into a more practical city-focused electric bicycle.
As much as I love high-performance electric mountain bikes, the reality is that most people aren’t spending their mornings bombing down mountain trails. They’re commuting to work, dropping kids off at school, and running errands.
And that’s where electric bicycles can make an even bigger difference.
The Amflow UE series seems to take a refreshingly comprehensive approach to urban riding. The powerful motor is nice, but I’m arguably more interested in the belt drive, integrated security, cargo capacity, automatic shifting, and built-in phone charging.
Those are the kinds of features that can make an electric bicycle genuinely easier to live with every day. And as someone who
actually commutes with an e-bike each day
as my main form of transportation, these bikes are really speaking to me!
If you ask me, it’s great to see another high-performance e-bike manufacturer recognizing that the future of electric bicycles isn’t just about riding farther and faster on trails. It’s also about making everyday transportation better for the less exciting type of riding, too.

title: Tesla's Semi Megacharger network hits 7 sites, far short of 37 goal
content:
Tesla Semi
Tesla Megacharger
Fred Lambert
| Nov 18 2026 - 7:43 am PT
Tesla has opened its first Semi Megacharger in Texas, an 8-stall station in Mesquite on the east side of Dallas. With it, Tesla’s map now lists 7 public Megacharger sites and 44 stalls for its electric truck.
That’s progress. But with six weeks left in 2026, it’s less than a fifth of the 37 sites Tesla planned to have open this year.
Texas finally gets one
Tesla Charging announced the new station on X on Tuesday night with its usual one-liner and a photo of the stalls at sunset:
New Tesla Megacharger: Mesquite, TX (8 stalls)
https://t.co/UsCFMyCjo7
Tesla’s map lists the site at 2175 S Town East Blvd in Mesquite, with eight Megachargers rated at up to 1.2 MW each.
Texas is where Tesla has the most riding on this network. When Tesla
added 64 Megacharger locations to its map in February
, Texas got 19 of the 66 planned sites, more than any other state. Mesquite is the first of them to go live, and several other Dallas–Fort Worth sites are still marked “coming soon.”
The Pilot truck stop rollout hasn’t reached Texas either. When Pilot opened its first Megacharger in Georgia in October, it named a Flying J in Fort Stockton, Texas, as one of the next sites. It’s still not live on Tesla’s map.
Tesla also isn’t alone in DFW. Greenlane, the truck charging joint venture between Daimler Truck, NextEra and BlackRock,
announced high-power sites in Dallas and Houston
in May, open to any electric truck with CCS and MCS connectors. Tesla now has a station operating in the metro.
The whole network fits in a short list
Here’s every public Megacharger currently live on Tesla’s map:
Bloomington, CA: 6 stalls
Vernon, CA: 6 stalls
Tulare, CA (Pilot/Flying J): 4 stalls
Conley, GA (south of Atlanta): 8 stalls
Ellabell, GA (Pilot, west of Savannah): 6 stalls
Hodgkins, IL (southwest of Chicago): 6 stalls
Mesquite, TX: 8 stalls
That’s 7 sites and 44 stalls in four states. When
we counted in early October
, there were four customer-facing sites with 26 stalls. Tulare opened the same week, Hodgkins came on November 10, and now Mesquite.
So Tesla is adding a site roughly every two weeks.
Tesla also runs private Megachargers for its own fleet at Giga Nevada and in Carson, California, and it sells Megachargers to fleets and depot operators through its business program. Forum Mobility switched on two at the Port of Long Beach earlier this month. None of those count toward the public network that Semi buyers without their own depot rely on.
The 37-site math doesn’t work
Tesla’s Q4 2025 shareholder report showed about 37 Megacharger sites for 2026. Semi program lead Dan Priestley has said Tesla wants 46 by early 2027.
To hit 37, Tesla would need to open 30 more sites in the next 43 days. At the current pace, it ends the year with around 10.
Pilot said in October that nine more of its sites were under construction, so a late burst is possible. But it would have to be a very big one.
And the trucks are starting to show up. Tesla
launched volume production of the Semi in September
at a Nevada factory it says can build 50,000 trucks a year, and it said last week that Chicago’s first 50 Semis are en route for delivery, a day after Hodgkins opened. Big fleets like that customer are installing their own depot chargers anyway, and most Semi charging will happen there. The public network is what lets a Semi leave its home region.

title: Volvo EWR150 Electric wheeled excavator gets to work in Luxembourg
content:
Electric Construction Equipment
Electric Heavy Machinery
Jo Borrás
| Nov 18 2026 - 7:34 am PT
As no-drip, low-noise job sites become more the global rule rather than the exception, Volvo’s incredibly versatile EWR150 Electric wheeled excavators are proving to be a smart addition to construction and municipal fleets – that’s proving true in Luxembourg, as well.
Volvo EWR150 Electric wheeled excavator
is helping the postage stamp nation of Luxembourg connect natural freshwater springs to a planned water reservoir, but the work has to be done in an existing groundwater protection zone, where even the smallest fuel spills or oil leaks could have serious consequences. An ideal opportunity, in other words,
for a battery electric machine like the EWR150 Electric to shine
“Sometimes I miss the sound of the engine,” says Thomas Weber, an operator on the project who’d previously worked with the conventional EWR150 wheeled excavator. “But the quieter operation of the EWR150 Electric is more beneficial for me, personally. Compared to the diesel equivalent, I find the performance and power to be identical.”
Volvo CE took to LinkedIn to share the work being done by the Luxemburgers at construction firm Elenz, touting the Volvo’s clean, quiet running in this highly environment.
For their part, Elenz executives are equally excited about the new machine. “Going electric is not a regulation, but a requirement for this particular job,” explains Christoph Schommer, Managing Director of Elenz. “We are thoroughly impressed by the EWR150 Electric. Its low noise level is a major advantage here. At the same time, the machine offers plenty of power and consistently delivers the same level of energy.”
The EWR150 Electric is built around a 270 kWh, 600V li-ion battery pack powering an electric drive motor that’s backed by a KERS-style hydraulic boom energy-recovery system that works like regenerative braking to extend the machine’s operating time. A 0.67 m³ (~0.9 yd³) bucket with 108.5-kN (~ 24,390 lb.) breakout force is standard, and offers a, 8.95 meter (~29 foot) maximum digging reach and 5.23 meter (~17 foot) digging depth. Volvo says the machine can typically operate for 8–10 hours depending on the application
Elenz is charging their EWR150 Electric overnight using a 32A L2 connection at a nearby sewage treatment plant, which also serves as the project office and a secure parking location for site equipment. By charging overnight, when Elenz’ crew isn’t working, the company has been able to integrate the big BEV without changing their existing work schedules.

title: BYD's luxury SUV pulled a nearly 400,000-pound jumbo jet on just two wheels [Video]
content:
Peter Johnson
| Nov 18 2026 - 7:15 am PT
Most SUVs are lucky to tow a small trailer without breaking a sweat.
new luxury SUV had a slightly bigger challenge: pulling a nearly 400,000-pound jumbo jet. And somehow, it did it on just two wheels. The video is worth a look.
BYD Denza Bao 5 vs jumbo jet, on two wheels
The Bao 5 made its European debut at the Goodwood Festival of Speed (FOS) in July, the first SUV from BYD’s “premium technology-focused” brand, Denza.
As Denza’s first SUV designed specifically for Europe, Stella Li, BYD’s executive vice president, said the company is “confident that the Bao 5 will be a huge hit,” offering the perfect mix of off-road ability, luxury, and advanced technology.
The SUV uses BYD’s DMO (Dual Mode Off-road) plug-in hybrid powertrain, which BYD said is the “world’s first off-road-dedicated hybrid architecture/”
BYD’s off-road PHEV powertrain features three electric motors (one on each axle and a third generator) and a 1.5L turbocharged engine, delivering a combined 536 horsepower (544 PS) and 560 lb-ft (760 Nm) of torque.
BYD boasted that “Those figures – well clear of PHEV rivals’ and comfortably more than conventional diesel SUVs’ – are enough for a 0-100km/h time of just 4.8 seconds.”
BYD Denza Bao 5 SUV pulls a Boeing 747 jumbo jet on two wheels (Source: Denza)
To top it off, BYD added a double wishbone front and rear suspension with its DiSus-P intelligent body system, plus front and rear intelligent electronic differential locks with millisecond-level response to improve traction and performance.
The Bao 5 is equipped with a 31.8 kWh BYD Blade Battery that delivers a pure-electric WLTP range of up to 56 miles (90 km). And on a full tank and a full charge, the WLTP combined range is 537 miles (835 km).
To prove the new luxury SUV’s capabilities, BYD put it to the ultimate test — towing a Boeing 747 jumbo jet using just two wheels.
BYD Denza Bao 5 SUV pulls a Boeing 747 jumbo jet on two wheels (Source: Denza)
While pulling a 180-tonne, or nearly 400,000-pound, jumbo jet on four wheels is impressive in itself, Denza’s engineers wanted to push it further, doing something never tried before to showcase its off-road DMO technology.
The Bao 5 was put to the test at Dunsfold Aerodrome airfield in Surrey, England. It successfully pulled the jumbo jet in each of its three runs: one on four wheels, one on three, and the last on just two wheels.
Combined, the SUV towed the 747 for a total of 1,600 meters, or close to a mile, which BYD said is about four laps around a standard-size athletic track.
BYD said the Bao 5 was a standard, production-spec Ultimate trim model, and the modifications were minimal.
A towing attachment was added, while the interior passenger seats were removed to make space for the 9,920 lb (4,500 kg) of ballast for the two-wheel pull test. In addition, Denza added small stabilizers to each axle so the vehicle remained balanced on two wheels.
After each run, the vehicle was inspected and confirmed to show no signs of stress on the powertrain, chassis, or tires.
The Bao 5 SUV normally has a towing capacity of over 5,500 lbs (2,500 kg), according to BYD’s Denza brand.

title: Current classics: Lord mayor of London's limo latest to go electric
content:
EV conversion
Rolls-Royce
Restomods
Electrogenic
Jo Borrás
| Nov 18 2026 - 4:31 am PT
If you wake up tomorrow as the esteemed Lord Mayor of London, you’ll want to make a properly
dignified
entrance. To make sure your arrival turns the right heads, Electrogenic has taken the Mayor’s 1973 Roll-Royce Phantom VI and turned it into a properly traditional standard-bearer with modern electric power.
The stately, stylish, and silent electric Rolls-Royce car made its public debut at last month’s Salon Privé weekend at Blenheim Palace, where it joined a growing fleet of classic Rollers that have received Elctrogenic’s electric conversion,
including the stunning Mulliner-bodied 1929 Phantom II that we covered back in 2023
For this project, Electrogenic carefully removed the internal combustion-based engine, transmission, and fuel system from the City of London Corporation’s official ’73 Phantom VI limo and replaced it with a 120 kW (~160 hp) electric motor putting out 310 Nm (~230 lb-ft) of torque. Sharp-eyed readers will note those numbers are significantly lower than what you’d expect from the 6.2L L410 V8 fitted with twin SU carburetors (as it was in the standard ’73 IV), but since those numbers were never officially published, we would say that the power available from the new electric drivetrain is similarly
adequate
for Mayoral use.
Power for the electric motor comes from a 62 kWh li-ion battery fitted under the
bonnet, and offers more than enough range to get the Lord Mayor to their appointments in and around the city.
Keeping it classy
Under the bonnet; by Electrogenic.
To ensure the heads of the heads of the city don’t bob in an undignified manner while on parade, Electrogenic added a “ceremonial” drive mode that trims power and torque and softens the throttle map, so the chauffeur can more easily hold the crawling pace demanded by civic processions and state occasions.
“We were honored to be asked to electrify this significant motor car, and to play a part in the City of London Corporation’s journey to net zero,” says Steve Drummond, chief executive of Electrogenic. “When it was launched in the late 1960s, the Rolls-Royce VI was the most refined and dignified limousine on the road. Now, thanks to electrification, its core character has been enhanced further: it is whisper quiet, effortless to drive with swift performance, and emits zero tailpipe emissions.”
Only 374 Phantom VIs were built between 1968 and 1990, with this 3 meter-long coach-built limousine having been commissioned during the mayoralty of Alderwoman Dame Susan Langley DBE, the 697th Lord Mayor of the City of London.
The Phantom was converted as part of the Corporation’s broader effort to achieve a net zero carbon emissions goal from its own operations in 2027
